staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line anchors below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `452a53a6c385e0caae91026e2008c9014f8f55a7`, but the prepared ARVO workspace used the commit above.

classification.classification_note: The saved sanitizer symptom is `negative-size-param` in `memmove()`, but the source-level defect is that malformed BGP UPDATE internal lengths are admitted and later collapse the layer below the 23-byte minimum that `setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` assumes. That lets `extendLayer()` compute an insertion index two bytes past the packet end.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42530091 (PcapPlusPlus): Negative-size-param found by fuzz target FuzzTargetNg [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42530091
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source / static parse of the staged `poc`
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 444-byte pcapng whose only packet is a Linux cooked IPv4/TCP packet to port 179. `TcpLayer::parseNextLayer()` dispatches the 269-byte TCP payload to BGP parsing, and vulnerable `BgpLayer::parseBgpLayer()` accepts four consecutive BGP UPDATE messages without validating UPDATE-specific internal lengths. The fourth UPDATE begins at raw packet offset 270, advertises common-header length 67, and stores withdrawn-routes length `0xfc00`. `getWithdrawnRoutesLength()` clamps that impossible field to the 46 bytes remaining in the message, so `getWithdrawnRoutes()` feeds bytes beginning with `0x00` into `parsePrefixAndIPData()` and produces an empty original withdrawn-routes vector. The fuzzer helper then calls `setWithdrawnRoutes()` with four synthetic routes, `clearWithdrawnRoutes()`, and finally `setWithdrawnRoutes()` with that empty vector; those edits shrink the malformed terminal UPDATE first to 36 bytes and then to the 21-byte minimum that still carries only the common header plus the withdrawn-routes-length field. When the helper next appends one NLRI prefix, `setNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` still asks `extendLayer()` to insert at fixed offset 23 (`sizeof(bgp_common_header) + 2*sizeof(uint16_t)`) even though the current layer is only 21 bytes long. Because this UPDATE is the last layer in the packet, `Packet::extendLayer()` computes an insertion index two bytes past `m_RawDataLen`, and `RawPacket::insertData()` reaches `memmove(..., m_RawDataLen - atIndex)` with size `-2`, matching the saved `AddressSanitizer: negative-size-param`. The fix adds `BgpUpdateMessageLayer::isDataValid()` and refuses UPDATE layers whose withdrawn-routes or path-attributes sublengths overrun the available message bytes.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `parseBgpLayer()` instantiates an UPDATE layer without validating that the withdrawn-routes and path-attributes sublengths fit inside `dataLen`, so later mutators operate on an internally inconsistent 67-byte UPDATE.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact return to `BgpUpdateMessageLayer::isDataValid(data, dataLen) ? new BgpUpdateMessageLayer(...) : nullptr;`, and `isDataValid()` rejects the witness because `withdrLen == 0xfc00` leaves no in-bounds location for the path-attributes-length field.

parser_admitted.description: The staged packet reaches the vulnerable parser path because the TCP destination port is 179, so `TcpLayer` dispatches the payload into BGP parsing instead of leaving it as a generic payload.
parser_admitted.condition: Static parsing of the staged `poc` shows the packet is IPv4/TCP with source port 53084, destination port 179, and a 269-byte TCP payload that vulnerable BGP parsing splits into four consecutive UPDATE messages. The crashing UPDATE is the fourth and final one.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted scalar is the fourth UPDATE's withdrawn-routes length. This method reads the raw bytes `fc 00` as 64512 and then clamps that impossible value to the 46 bytes remaining in the 67-byte message.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Static parsing of the staged witness shows that the fourth BGP UPDATE at raw packet offset 270 stores common-header length `0x0043` (67) and withdrawn-routes bytes `fc 00`. On this tree, `getHeaderLen()` returns 67 for that layer, so this method materializes `res == 64512` and the later comparison against `headerLen - 21 == 46` reduces the effective withdrawn-routes span to 46 bytes.
tainted_value_origin.note: That clamped 46-byte span is later reused as the amount of data to erase from the malformed UPDATE, which is why the layer collapses below the minimum size assumed by the NLRI setter.

coarse_trace.summary: TCP port 179 dispatch admits the payload into BGP parsing, and vulnerable `parseBgpLayer()` materializes the final 67-byte segment as a `BgpUpdateMessageLayer` without UPDATE-specific length validation.
The fourth UPDATE's forged withdrawn-routes field `0xfc00` is clamped to 46 bytes, and parsing that slice stops immediately on leading byte `0x00`, leaving the original withdrawn-routes vector empty.
The helper's withdraw-route edits first shorten the malformed UPDATE from 67 to 36 bytes and then, after `clearWithdrawnRoutes()`, to the 21-byte minimum with zero withdrawn routes.
On the shortened 21-byte layer the NLRI accessor reports no data, but the setter still tries to insert one new `/24` prefix at fixed offset 23.

Because the malformed UPDATE is the last layer and only 21 bytes long, `extendLayer()` translates offset 23 into a packet index two bytes past `m_RawDataLen`, and `insertData()` reaches the saved `memmove(size=-2)` sink.

fine_trace.function: pcpp::BgpLayer::parseBgpLayer(unsigned char*, unsigned long, pcpp::Layer*, pcpp::Packet*)
fine_trace.code:
case 2: // UPDATE
	return new BgpUpdateMessageLayer(data, dataLen, prevLayer, packet);
fine_trace.note: Source and parser-admission step. The fourth TCP-payload segment is 67 bytes long, carries `messageType == 2`, and is therefore materialized as `BgpUpdateMessageLayer` without any check that its UPDATE-specific sublengths are consistent with those 67 bytes. The staged fix inserts `BgpUpdateMessageLayer::isDataValid(data, dataLen)` exactly here.

Tainted-length step. For the malformed final UPDATE, `headerLen == 67` and the withdrawn-routes bytes are `fc 00`, so `res == 64512`. This guard clamps the effective withdrawn-routes span to `67 - 21 == 46` bytes.

When `getWithdrawnRoutes()` passes the 46-byte slice from step 2, the first byte is `0x00`, which matches none of the accepted prefix widths {32, 24, 16, 8}. The parser breaks immediately and leaves the original `withdrawnRoutes` vector empty.

The helper appends four fixed routes before this first setter call, so `newWithdrawnRoutesDataLen == 15` while the current malformed withdrawn-routes span from step 2 is 46. The shorten branch removes 31 bytes from the final UPDATE and rewrites the BGP common-header length from 67 down to 36.

`clearWithdrawnRoutes()` invokes the same setter with an empty vector, so `newWithdrawnRoutesDataLen == 0` against the current 15-byte section from step 4. That removes the remaining withdrawn-routes bytes, zeroes the stored withdrawn-routes-length field, and leaves the final UPDATE at the 21-byte minimum. The subsequent `setWithdrawnRoutes(withdrawnRoutes)` call is a no-op because step 3 left the original `withdrawnRoutes` vector empty, so the layer stays 21 bytes long.

On the shortened layer from step 5, `headerLen == 21`, which is smaller than the 23-byte minimum needed for both the withdrawn-routes-length and path-attributes-length fields. This accessor therefore returns 0, and `getNetworkLayerReachabilityInfo()` leaves `nlriVec` empty.

The helper appends one fixed `/24` prefix (`40.1.1.0`) to the empty `nlriVec`, so `newNlriDataLen == 4`. Because steps 5-6 left the layer with no withdrawn routes, no path attributes, and no NLRI, all current lengths are 0. This code still uses fixed insertion offset `19 + 2 + 2 == 23` and calls `extendLayer(23, 4)` without checking that the current layer is at least 23 bytes long.

For the terminal UPDATE, the current layer length is only 21 bytes from step 5, but step 7 supplies `offsetInLayer == 23`. Because this malformed UPDATE is the last layer in the packet, `indexToInsertData` resolves to the current raw-packet end plus 2 bytes.

format.name: pcapng / Linux cooked IPv4/TCP/BGP
format.contract: This exact staged `poc` is a 444-byte pcapng with one 337-byte Linux-cooked packet whose TCP destination port is 179 and whose 269-byte TCP payload is parsed as four consecutive BGP UPDATE messages of lengths 68, 68, 66, and 67. The witness condition is the fourth UPDATE at payload offset 202 / raw packet offset 270: it carries marker bytes `ff...ff`, common-header length `0x0043`, type `0x02`, and withdrawn-routes bytes `fc 00`, so vulnerable code clamps the current withdrawn-routes span to 46 bytes, parses no original routes, shrinks the last UPDATE to 21 bytes via the helper's clear/restore sequence, and then reaches the saved NLRI insertion at offset 23 that produces `negative-size-param (size=-2)`.
